Set 1.text: You are given a difficult problem for which your teacher has not provided a standard method. What would you most naturally do first?
Suppose you are learning about artificial intelligence. What interests you most about AI?
Your team must choose between two project ideas. One is safer and likely to succeed; the other is more ambitious but uncertain. What would you consider first?
options: The project with stronger evidence and logic.
The project my team members feel more comfortable with.
The project where I can combine the strengths of both options.
The ambitious project if it is worth the risk.

Set 1.text: You have 3 major assignments, 1 coaching/classes and an upcoming examination in the same week.

options: Ask for feedback from a teacher or evaluator.
Try a different approach next time.
Move on quickly to the next task.

Set 1.text: On a scale of 1-10, how comfortable are you with making an important decision without simply following what your friends or family expect you to do?
When a group project faces a major roadblock, what is your natural instinct to jump in and fix?
If you had two free weeks and full funding, what would you spend your time doing?
options: Building: Coding, assembling, or fixing something.
Investigating: Researching, analyzing, or solving a problem.
Creating: Writing, filming, designing, or making art.
Helping: Teaching, mentoring, or helping others.

Set 1.text: If a newspaper featured your ₹10,000 project, which headline would make you proudest?

Set 1.text: Your school is building a smart city. Which role interests you most?
options: Designer: Designing the look and experience.
Mentor: Helping people and the team.
Leader: Pitching ideas and leading the project.
Organizer: Managing data, budgets, and timelines.

Set 1.text: Think of a moment that gives you instant happiness or satisfaction. What did you enjoy most?
options: Seeing something I built or fixed work.
Finding the answer to a difficult problem.
Creating a new idea or design.
Getting people excited about my idea.

Set 1.text: Which extracurricular activity would you most likely choose?
Which problem would you most enjoy solving?
options: How can we make this physical device work better?
Why is this happening, and what evidence can explain it?
How can we communicate this idea creatively?
How can we help people cooperate better?
How can we persuade people to adopt this idea?
How can we organise the information so that errors are reduced?

Set 1.text: You get a free month to explore a career area. Which would you choose?
Your group is launching something big. Which role do you claim immediately?
options: The Builder - assemble the tech and make it run.
The Investigator - research the facts and run the numbers.
The Creative - design the vibe, visuals, and content.
The Anchor - check in on teammates and keep morale high.
The Shot-Caller - pitch the vision and make executive calls.
The Architect - set deadlines, track tasks, and keep files clean.

Set 1.text: If you could build serious real-world experience right now, what area would you dive into?
options: Robotics, machine tuning, and physical fabrication.
Data modeling, algorithmic research, and deep-dive analysis.
Brand identity, motion graphics, and creative production.
Mental health advocacy, youth mentoring, and community aid.
Startup / pitching business ventures, marketing, and team leadership.
Financial planning, resource management, and clean data systems.

Set 1.text: Which statement sounds most like you?
options: I like understanding why things happen.
I like creating and expressing ideas.
I like working with and helping people.
I like influencing, leading or building things.
I like organizing information and making systems work efficiently.

Set 1.text: If you had to choose one professional skill to develop now:

A retailer purchases a product for ₹5,000 and marks up its price such that after offering two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on the marked price, he still earns a net profit of 8%. If he changes his strategy and offers a single flat discount of 25% on the same marked price, what will be his new selling price (and corresponding profit percentage)?
Find the next number: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___

In a software company, the ratio of senior engineers to junior engineers was 4:7. After 12 senior engineers were promoted and left the team, and 24 new junior engineers were hired, the ratio of senior engineers to junior engineers became 1:3. How many total engineers (senior and junior combined) were initially in the team?
A test has 80 questions. A student answers 60 correctly. What percentage did the student answer correctly?

Five project leads-A, B, C, D, and E-are seated in a row facing North. C is sitting to the immediate right of E. A is not sitting at either extreme end. B sits second to the left of D. Exactly two people sit between A and E. Which of the following represents the exact left-to-right order of the leads?
Find the next pair of letters in the series: AZ, CX, FU, JQ, ___

Premises:
All architects are creative.
Some engineers are architects.
No creative person is careless.

Which of the following conclusions must be true?
Rigid : Flexible :: Chaotic : ?
Which word does NOT belong in the group?
Find the sequence: ○▲ → ▲■■ → ■●●● → ●◆◆◆◆ → ? Which option should come next?
You are facing East. You turn left, then turn right, then turn right again. Which direction are you facing?

A student has 24 hours in a day: Sleep 8h, School 7h, Study 5h, Travel 2h, Other 2h. If the student reduces sleep by 1 hour and uses that time for study, what percentage of the day will then be spent on study and school combined?
You discover an AI tool that can do something you normally spend hours doing. What do you do first?
options: Find new ways to use it.
Think about where it could lead.
Try it on a real task.
Show others what it can do.
Ask friends how they would use it.

Set 1.text: You and your friends want to start a YouTube/Instagram channel. What excites you most?
options: Planning how the channel could grow.

Set 1.text: You are playing a new game and keep losing at the same level. What do you do?
options: Study the level and plan ahead.
Keep practising until I crack it.
Play with someone and learn together.

Set 1.text: A viral trend suddenly becomes popular. What are you most likely to do?
options: Find out why it became popular.
Think about where the trend is going.
See what people are saying about it.

Set 1.text: Your friends ask you to plan a weekend experience. What would you naturally do?
options: Plan the experience around what could happen.

Set 1.text: You are given ₹50,000 to create something for your generation. What would you do?
options: Create something people haven't seen before.
Turn the idea into a working product.
Build something people would follow or support.
Create something that brings people together.

Set 1.text: Two group members are arguing over opposing ideas for an assignment. How do you respond?
options: Compare both ideas using facts and logic.
Combine both ideas into a fresh third concept.
Align both ideas with the project's bigger goal.
Pick the quickest option to start work immediately.
Persuade both sides to compromise and decide.
Listen empathetically and restore team harmony.

Set 1.text: You have a free weekend with no tests or homework. How would you prefer to spend it?
options: Solve logic puzzles, code, or read complex topics.
Write, draw, edit videos, or redesign personal space.
Explore future tech trends, startups, or career goals.
Organize your room, plan calendars, or complete tasks.
Join a debate, network, or organize a student meetup.
Hang out with friends, listen to stories, or help others.

Set 1.text: When making a major decision about your future stream or college path, what matters most?
options: Deep intellectual challenge and logical fit.
Freedom to innovate, design, and create.
Strong future scope, growth, and long-term relevance.
Clear, stable path with predictable milestones.
Alignment with personal values and positive social impact.

Set 2.text: You are asked to solve a problem at school, but no instructions are provided. What would you most likely do?
options: Understand the situation and identify the root problem.
Brainstorm several new ways to solve it.
Predict the future outcome of each option first.
Pick the most practical option and start fixing it.
Take charge, rally a team, and divide the work.
Gather everyone's input to reach a group consensus.

Set 2.text: Your team has to create an exhibition stall for a major school fest. What is your first instinct?
options: Calculate the budget and analyze past fest data.
Plan how it benefits your future portfolio.
Make a deadline checklist and start setup.
Pitch to teachers to get the best location.
Assign roles so everyone is happy and comfortable.

Set 2.text: A major presentation file gets corrupted 1 hour before submission. What do you do?
options: Inspect the file structure to fix the glitch.
Sketch a quick, novel way to deliver the topic.
Reassess the goal and focus on key slides only.
Lock in and retype the lost content fast.
Talk to the teacher to get an extension.
Calm down the team and split the remaining work.

Set 2.text: You have to choose between two opportunities. What influences you most?
options: Which one lets you take responsibility.
How it affects the people involved.

Set 2.text: Your teacher asks the class to improve something in school. What interests you most?
options: Imagining how it could work better.

Set 2.text: When picking a topic for an independent research paper, what type appeals to you most?
options: A technical or scientific problem needing data analysis.
An open-ended topic allowing original, creative ideas.
An emerging trend exploring the world's 10-year future.
A practical topic with clear steps and measurable outcomes.
A social or political issue where you argue a strong view.
A community topic focused on human psychology and helping people.

Set 2.text: You received a lower grade than expected on an important test. What is your immediate reaction?
options: Review the paper to spot exact mistakes and errors.
Try a new, creative study strategy next time.
Re-evaluate your overall study roadmap for the year.
Set a strict timetable and double your practice hours.
Speak with the teacher for feedback and extra credit.
Discuss it with a friend, process emotions, and stay positive.

Set 2.text: Fast forward 5 years. What kind of daily work environment sounds best to you?
options: A quiet environment focusing on complex analytics and logic.
A creative studio with design and experimentation freedom.
A strategic setup planning long-term growth and direction.
A structured team focused on clear targets and efficiency.
A high-impact company where you lead, present, and influence.
A supportive space focused on teaching, counseling, or helping.

Set 2.text: When introduced to a completely new topic or skill, how do you learn it best?
options: Break down core concepts step-by-step until the logic clicks.
Experiment freely and find unique ways to apply it.
Connect it to real-world trends and the big picture.
Practice repeatedly with structured guidelines until mastered.
Explain or teach the concept to someone else.
Learn through group discussions and team exercises.

Set 1.text: If you had to teach someone how to do something, what is your go-to method?
options: Breaking it down through speech or writing.
Walking through the data, math, and step-by-step logic.
Drawing a sketch, diagram, or mental map.

Set 1.text: Which activity would you most enjoy?
options: Understanding how other people think or feel.
Reflecting on your own decisions and behaviour.
Observing animals, plants or the natural environment.

Set 1.text: When explaining a difficult concept to someone, what are you most likely to do?
options: Explain it using words and examples.
Draw a diagram or visual representation.

Set 1.text: Which challenge would you choose?
options: Analyse how a group of people is behaving.
Write an article explaining an issue.

Set 1.text: Which ability would you most like to develop further?
What clears your head faster than anything else?
options: Audio - losing yourself in rhythms, beats, or lyrics.
Connection - talking it out with someone you trust.
Outdoors - spending time in open spaces and nature.

Set 1.text: Which combination sounds most like your natural strengths?
options: Visual: Spatial design, art & aesthetic layout
Kinesthetic: Hands-on fabrication, tools & physical agility

Set 1.text: If you had to choose between these two opportunities, which would you prefer?
options: A stable career with predictable growth.
A less predictable career with greater opportunity to create something new.

Set 1.text: Which achievement would mean more to you?
options: Becoming highly skilled and respected in my field.
Making a meaningful difference to other people.

Set 1.text: Which would motivate you more?
options: Being given freedom to decide how to complete my work.
Being given a challenging target and having to prove that I can achieve it.

Set 1.text: Which future situation would you prefer?
options: Leading people and making important decisions.
Becoming an expert and solving complex problems.

Set 1.text: Rate the importance of financial security in your future career.
Rate the importance of doing work that you genuinely find meaningful or interesting.

options: Visual Synthesis: Flowcharts, concept mind-maps, and formula sheets.
Written Revision: Active reading, summarizing, and writing out detailed notes.
Peer Teaching: Explaining concepts aloud to a friend or study partner.

Set 1.text: Rate how strongly you prefer learning by actually doing something rather than only reading or listening about it.
You realise you're getting irritated during a group project because things aren't going your way. What's most true for you?
options: I notice the irritation building up almost immediately, even before I say anything.
I can usually calm myself down before it affects how I act.
I also notice when the irritation is affecting how my teammates feel.
I say something to the team so we can sort it out together, instead of staying quiet.

Set 1.text: Your marks suddenly fall in a subject you normally do well in. What's your first instinct?
options: I try to name exactly what I'm feeling about it - disappointment, worry, frustration.
I give myself a set amount of time to feel bad about it, then move to fixing it.
I think about how my parents or teacher might feel about it too.
I talk to a teacher, friend or parent about what happened.

Set 1.text: A close friend strongly disagrees with something you believe. How do you usually handle it?
options: I'm aware of exactly how strongly I feel about my own view before I even respond.
I keep my tone calm even if I feel strongly, so it doesn't turn into a fight.
I try to understand why they see it so differently before reacting.
I look for a way we can both walk away from the conversation feeling heard.

Set 1.text: You have several important deadlines at once and start feeling overwhelmed. What do you do?
options: I notice the overwhelm building before it turns into panic.
I break the work into smaller pieces so I don't spiral.
I pay attention to whether the people around me are stressed by this too.
I ask someone for help or to share the load rather than struggling alone.

Set 1.text: Your school wants to reduce students' dependence on last-minute exam preparation. Which idea would you most like to develop?
options: A completely new approach to exam preparation.
A system combining several of these ideas.

Set 1.text: You are given a problem but very little information about how to solve it. What would you prefer?
options: Generate several possible solutions before choosing one.
Combine existing ideas into something new.

options: Ask others to challenge my thinking.
Start again using what I learned.

options: Decided: I know what I want to pursue.
